clue.text: You should keep well away from this

definitions.text: You should keep well away from this

parts.words: You should keep well away from this
parts.note: reads like advice to avoid something dangerous, but 'keep well away' also means stay away while you are well, i.e. only the ill belong there

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of some hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep well away' sounds like 'avoid it'; read it as 'stay off it while healthy': only an invalid uses it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is where a patient lies while ill, so a healthy person has no business in it.

clue.text: Our group elevated source of luminance in darkness or luminance in daytime

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, so in a down answer the letters read upwards

parts.note: us is our group

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for darkness

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle about where light comes from, day or night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns US upwards to SU; 'in' puts L, from 'source of luminance', into NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The light reaching us during the day comes from the sun.

clue.text: Shellfish with feathers bringing in start of pesticide restriction

indicators.note: bringing in means the letter is taken in between the shellfish and feathers

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
down is soft fine feathers

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Shellfish and birds caught up in limits on pesticide use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just links; 'feathers' is a noun here (soft plumage), not a verb, and 'bringing in' sets the pesticide's first letter between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a firm restriction imposed by authorities.

clue.text: Intelligence beginning to rise earlier in Scots children

indicators.note: earlier means the letter is shifted to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: bairns is the Scots word for children

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Clever Scottish children showing early promise.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRNS is Scots for children. 'beginning to rise' is R, which moves 'earlier', two places forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plenty of grey matter means having intellect; the plural is the informal word for cleverness.

clue.text: Despair re: crooked hangings

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so the letters are set askew

explanation.surface: Someone despairing over curtains that hang crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains and drapes are fabric hangings at windows or walls.

clue.text: Half of that's covered by loud noise

indicators.note: half of says take only the first two of the four letters of that

parts.note: something covered by another thing lies under it

explanation.surface: Something half-hidden beneath a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes TH, the front half of THAT; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crash that follows lightning is the classic loud noise of a storm.

clue.text: Time's perfect, extracting energy of sea movements

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: extracting means pulling out the energy letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A perfect moment to harness wave power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracting energy' removes E from IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective describing the rise and fall of the ocean governed by the moon.

clue.text: Open French articles about deer

indicators.note: about means going round, so the articles surround the deer

parts.note: un and le are French articles
a buck is a male deer

explanation.surface: French grammar book opened at a page about deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' is a verb here, not an adjective; 'about' wraps the two articles round the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing a belt or strap's fastening is a way to release or unfasten it.

clue.text: Skin or inner section of flounder, maybe

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fishmonger asking about the skin or inner part of a flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounder' looks like the start of the definition, but its last three letters join MA of 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means skin, or specifically the dermis, the inner layer beneath the epidermis.

clue.text: One's climbing in gnarled tree — find a different spot

indicators.note: in places the climbing pair within the twisted tree letters
gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted
climbing means going up, which in a down answer reverses the letters

parts.note: one is I, and 's is 'is', giving IS

explanation.surface: A climber in a twisted tree looking for a better place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnarled' makes RETE; 'climbing' reverses, since this is a down answer; 'in' sets the reversed pair inside. The 's of 'One's' is 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To move something such as a building or business to another location.

clue.text: Any swirling stuff from the Sahara will trap the French in part of old Africa

indicators.note: swirling suggests the letters of 'Any' being whirled into a new order
to trap is to hold something inside, so the desert stuff closes round the French word

parts.note: the Sahara is a desert, full of sand
la is French for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: A sandstorm blowing across a colonial-era African territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' gives NYA; 'will trap' gives SALAND. 'Stuff from the Sahara' is a playful definition of the desert material.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the British colonial name of the country now called Malawi.

clue.text: Tenders to include run for poultry?

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the offers hold the letter for run

parts.note: tenders are offers or bids
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Keepers of a chicken run tending their flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenders' and 'run' both pretend to belong to a farmyard; tenders are bids here. The question mark marks poultry as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry such as hens and ducks are examples of feathered creatures, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I plan to see off a naughty child

indicators.note: off means the letter a is taken away from the word for plan

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to get rid of a badly behaved kid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is padding linking the pieces; 'off a' removes the A from MAP to leave MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous little devil, used of a cheeky youngster.

clue.text: Reflected an oddball in embroidery?

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric, signalling these letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A mirror image of an eccentric person stitched into a piece of embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddball' is the anagram signal on REFLECTED AN; the question mark shows embroidery is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Embroidery is one kind of sewing skill done with a needle, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Gangster over and over again avoiding jinx

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out the two letters for 'over and over again'

parts.note: a hoodoo is a jinx or bad-luck charm

indicators.note: and over again says the over letter appears a second time

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A mobster who keeps steering clear of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over and over again' is two Os, which come off the end of HOODOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood is slang for a hoodlum, a gangster or thug.

clue.text: I note marine industry not initially taking a breather

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the industry word is dropped

parts.note: whaling is an industry carried out at sea

explanation.surface: A sea worker pausing for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes the W from WHALING. The definition puns: a breather is normally a rest, here literally drawing breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing air into the lungs is literally taking a breath.

clue.text: Bacon and mash dished up — something for the traveller

indicators.note: food dished up is prepared and served, so these letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hearty meal served to someone on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dished up' is the anagram signal on BACON MASH; 'and' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire was Victorian transport for passengers.

clue.text: A couple of monarchs appearing in state history

indicators.note: appearing in places the article and two kings inside the state word

parts.note: a nation is a state
R (rex or regina) stands for a monarch, so two give RR

explanation.surface: Two kings or queens featuring in a country's past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' puts the letters after the first letter of the state word. 'History' means a telling, not the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A history in the sense of a story or account told, a telling of events.

clue.text: Dance taken up around this month in part of Ireland

indicators.note: around means the dance letters go round this month's abbreviation
taken up means lifted, so in a down answer the dance is read upwards

parts.note: a reel is a lively dance
inst., short for instant, means of this month in old letter style

explanation.surface: A dance revived this month in an Irish province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns REEL to LEER, which goes 'around' INST, the old commercial abbreviation for 'this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the four provinces of Ireland, containing Dublin.

clue.text: Writer to run off with long-abandoned wife

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
to elope is to run off secretly to marry

explanation.surface: An author who has run away with someone, leaving a spouse behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a deserted wife; she is the faithful wife in Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus left this wife alone for twenty years while he fought and wandered home.

clue.text: Articles in English and German initially sycophantic about film director

parts.note: an is an English indefinite article and der a German definite article

indicators.note: initially picks out just the first letter of the word sycophantic

parts.note: on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A director praised in two languages by a fawning critic.
explanation.walkthrough: AN (English) and DER (German) are the articles, then S from 'initially' and ON for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindsay and Wes are both movie-makers with this surname.

clue.text: Expecting no payment, runs into charge

indicators.note: into means the letter for runs goes inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone working for nothing who still ends up hit with a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like the definition but supplies FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gratis means asking for nothing in return.

clue.text: Pleased one gets bit of mint? Not mint

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is its first letter

parts.note: mint means brand new, so not mint is second-hand

explanation.surface: Someone happy with a piece of a sweet, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' is used twice: its first letter M, then 'Not mint' as in stamps or cars, which are not new.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained or tickled means feeling pleased.

clue.text: Poet watching when Republican enters

indicators.note: enters means the Republican letter goes inside the watching word

parts.note: a vigil is a period of watching

explanation.surface: A poet observing as a Republican politician comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts R inside VIGIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman author of the Aeneid is a celebrated classical poet.

clue.text: Reminder of being late? Mark's more on time, possibly

parts.note: M stands for the mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: possibly signals an alternative arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether their watch makes them more punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MORE ON TIME. 'Late' means dead, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase, 'remember you must die', names an object reminding one of death; 'late' means deceased.

clue.text: Low rains emptied uplands

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: emptied means removing the inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Little rain falling on high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective opposed to 'uplands', but it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorland is open, high, uncultivated country, often heath.

clue.text: Postponed as soon as receiving intervention from Independent

indicators.note: receiving intervention means having something put in the middle

parts.note: once means as soon as

explanation.surface: A plan delayed the moment a newspaper interfered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' nods at the newspaper running the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan kept in the freezer is deferred for later, an idiom for delay.

clue.text: Test curtailed, then recalled for cancellation

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run the other way
curtailed means having its tail cut off, losing its last letter

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: An exam cut short and then called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the last letter of EXAM, leaving EXA, and 'recalled' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something the chop means scrapping it, a newspaper sense of abolition or cuts.

clue.text: English explorer hauling bed into street

indicators.note: into places the bed word inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A polar explorer dragging his sledge bed down a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hauling' only links the pieces, echoing man-hauled sledges.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott led the doomed British expedition to the South Pole.

clue.text: Coin and ingot melted down, concealing identity

indicators.note: metal melted down is recast in a new shape, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: Stolen coins and bullion being melted so they cannot be traced.
explanation.definitionFit: Going about in disguise means hiding who one really is.

clue.text: Daughter's reluctance to get engaged having no initial merit

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: having no initial means the first letter of the reluctance word goes

parts.note: reserve is a reluctance to engage with others

explanation.surface: A daughter's hesitancy about marrying, apparently undeserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get engaged' suggests marriage, but means social involvement: reserve is shyness. 'having no initial' removes its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be worthy of something is to have earned it; the verb sense fits.

clue.text: Equilibrium: an Introduction to Composure is in package

indicators.note: is in places the article and initial letter inside the package word

parts.note: a bale is a large bundle or package

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Like the title of a self-help book on keeping calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' sets the article and C inside the package word; the colon after the definition is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of steadiness, with forces evenly matched, is a synonym of equilibrium.
